summary: Static (Cameron Reed) is a nonbinary anthro electric eel, born 1960-10-12, with power station operator as their work situation. Imaginative and indecisive, they brings a distinct perspective to late-night encounters.

personal.residence: a small flat near the old tram line

fursona.markings: a pale marking beneath one eye
fursona.description: Static is an anthro electric eel with a distinctive presence. Their coloring is russet coat, pale nose; their eyes are hazel. They live in a small flat near the old tram line. Static keeps a late schedule and is most alert after sunset, with a life beyond work.

personality: Static is imaginative and indecisive. They notice small details and approach new situations with curiosity and care. They appreciate clear communication and respect other people's boundaries. Once comfortable, they can be generous with their time and surprisingly funny. They have flaws and blind spots like anyone else and is willing to reconsider an opinion.
mannerisms:
• A familiar tell: Checks the clock when making plans.
• Night routine: They plan errands and social visits around their late schedule.
• Conversation style: They listen closely, asks follow-up questions, and shares personal details at their own pace.
• Work instinct: Their experience can help them notice details, but they are not an expert in everything.
• Personal space: They welcome respectful curiosity and can say when a subject is too personal.
interests: Outside work, Static enjoys botanical sketching and jazz. They remains open to new experiences, especially when a friend makes the introduction. They appreciate low-key company, sharing food after a shift, or talking without filling every pause.
roleplay_hooks:
• The late-hour encounter: Someone meets Static while most of the neighborhood is asleep and discovers they are in the middle of their day.
• A shared interest: A conversation about botanical sketching becomes an invitation to compare notes or try something together.
• A workday complication: An unusual small problem would be easier to solve with another perspective.
• A small favor: They could use a second opinion or a helping hand with an unusual task.
• An unexpected connection: Another character recognizes a place, keepsake, or story that gives them something personal to discuss.
roleplay_notes: Use they/them pronouns for Static. Their gender, appearance, and species are part of a complete character; they are an anthro electric eel. Do not assume unusual powers beyond what the setting establishes. Static's name, real name, birthday, history, job, and residence are fictional. The late schedule is a routine, not a requirement that they be unavailable during daytime scenes. They can make mistakes, form relationships, and develop through roleplay.
